Class PreLobbyController

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am56.view.TUI.controllers.BaseTUIController
it.polimi.ingsw.am56.view.TUI.controllers.PreLobbyController
All Implemented Interfaces:
UpdateHandler, MessageVisitor
public class PreLobbyController extends BaseTUIController
TUI pre-lobby screen: it queries the server for the current state and then runs one of three flows depending on that state — create a new game, join an open lobby, or reconnect to a game that is already in progress (the persistence/resume case, e.g. after a server restart). It collects the player's nickname (and, when creating/joining, the totem color), validating them against the names/colors already taken, and sends the matching request. It then advances to the LobbyController when a lobby state arrives, or straight to the GameController when a game snapshot arrives (the reply to a successful reconnect).

    • visit

      public void visit(LobbyStateMessage message)
      Transitions to the lobby screen — but only once this client has actually joined. LobbyStateMessage is broadcast to every connected client whenever any player joins or creates the game, so a client still sitting in the pre-lobby (no nickname chosen yet, not logged in) would otherwise be pulled into the game without having joined. We therefore advance only after this client has actually sent its own join/create request and its nickname appears among the lobby's players; otherwise the broadcast concerns other players and is ignored.
      Parameters:
      message - the lobby state

    • handleReconnected

      public void handleReconnected()
      On reconnection, refreshes the pre-lobby state on this same controller — it must not create a new PreLobbyController. The pre-lobby flow reads input with a blocking scanner on the main thread: if a player is mid-prompt (e.g. choosing a totem color) when the server drops, that flow is still parked on System.in. Re-entering a fresh controller here (on the reconnect thread) would start a second flow reading the same scanner, so the two would fight over the input and the original one would be orphaned, leaving the player stuck. Instead we just re-request the state: visit(PreLobbyStateMessage) updates the fields (releasing onEnter() if it is still waiting, and refreshing gameExists / gameInProgress) and the already-running flow proceeds against the reconnected server.
